newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria may get up to 200,000T Kazakhstan wheat.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria may get up to 200,000T Kazakhstan wheat.

text.p: Bulgaria, suffering a severe grain shortage, hopes to receive some 100,000-200,000 tonnes of Kazakh wheat in exchange for forgiving part of Kazakhstan's debt, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister said on Wednesday.
Doncho Konakchiev said Kazakhstan owed "tens of millions of dollars" to Bulgaria's construction firm Glavbolgarstroy for construction works there.
"We will receive Kazakh wheat in return for part of the Glavbolgarstroy payment," Konakchiev told reporters.
He said the Kazakh grain crop this year was some 14-15 million tonnes and their annual exports were 4-5 million tonnes.
"Experts from the two countries will prepare the deal and I think that supplies of some 100,000-200,000 tonnes would not be a problem for Kazakhstan," Konakchiev said.

On Tuesday, he met visiting Kazakh parliamentarians, who he said had shown great interest in Bulgaria's experience in building. Bulgarian building firms will participate in a Kazakh tender for building a new capital, Konakchiev said.
High Bulgarian wheat exports in 1995 and record low yields this year due to poor weather and a lack of fertilisers have triggered serious bread shortages.
Agriculture ministry officials said this week Bulgaria, which is short of cash, was looking for barter deals to help meet its grain needs.
Its wheat supplies stand at 130,000 tonnes while domestic wheat consumption is 500,000 tonnes a year, officials say.

Last week, Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee for the import of 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat after state-owned Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line due to unfavourable conditions. --Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
